feed.title: AVAVA Homes & Estates — the journal
feed.subtitle: Market reports, legal changes and what we learned refusing files.

entry.title: The short-let licence review, street by street
entry.summary: Six districts lost their tourism licence in July. We mapped the addresses that keep it and how asking prices reacted in the four weeks after.

entry.title: The attic that was never there
entry.summary: A 210 m² townhouse in the old town, listed for eleven months by two agencies. The top floor did not appear on any permit issued since 1904.

entry.title: Staged payments on off-plan purchases
entry.summary: The three clauses that protect a buyer when a delivery date slips — and the one developers quietly remove from the standard contract.

entry.title: Issue 14 — the quarter in thirty-eight cities
entry.summary: Medians barely moved, but the discount sellers accepted widened with every price band. The full spread, city by city and street by street.

entry.title: Restoration grants in the historic centres
entry.summary: Up to thirty per cent of the works covered in Palermo and Porto. What qualifies, what does not, and how long the paperwork really takes.

entry.title: Eight metres that cost forty thousand
entry.summary: The deed said a hundred and four square metres. The laser said ninety-six. What happens between those two numbers and a signature.

entry.title: Notary practice across four countries, compared
entry.summary: Who checks what, what it costs, and where a buyer is genuinely protected rather than merely charged.

entry.title: Where the days-to-offer number actually comes from
entry.summary: Portals count from the day a listing is republished. We count from first publication, which is why our forty-one looks worse than their nineteen.

entry.title: Two lenders, one file, forty-two basis points
entry.summary: We sent the same complete application to eleven lenders. The spread on identical paperwork was wider than a year of rate movement.

entry.title: What a roof actually costs in the old town
entry.summary: Nine completed jobs, invoices seen, from a patch repair to a full replacement with the beams out.

entry.title: The charge nobody mentioned
entry.summary: A clean-looking apartment with an eleven-year-old community debt attached to the unit rather than the owner.

entry.title: Energy certificates: the letter and the bill
entry.summary: We compared the rating on file with a year of real consumption for two hundred flats. The letter is a weak predictor.
